lanes.name: depth-first-qa frames
lanes.what: pixel diff of the replayed route against base, 0.1% of pixels per frame

lanes.name: depth-first-qa failed requests
lanes.what: requests that failed while the route played

lanes.name: depth-first-qa outside requests
lanes.what: requests to hosts outside the game folder

lanes.name: depth-first-qa ready gate
lanes.what: no canvas or no quiet network before the route starts

lanes.name: depth-first-qa randomness count
lanes.what: Math.random calls seen during the run

source.note: Hero, floor and background separate by lightness first; a grayscale capture must still separate them.
Ambient, diffuse and specular terms; the dark side is never fully black.
Web 3D assets ship as glTF 2.0, one .glb per asset, validated before upload.
Input arrives as action names, not physical keys, read in one handler.
Audio opens on the first user gesture.
Simulation runs a fixed-step step function; rendering only reads the state.
Saved data carries an integer version and old-version samples must still load.
The same input record must give the same state on every browser and device.
A material template must compile without errors and draw one frame in the engine.

risks.title: Texture and loader color space after the colorSpace switch
risks.breaks: r152 replaced Texture.encoding with Texture.colorSpace (default NoColorSpace) and turned ColorManagement on, so textures on loaded models that relied on the old encoding read as linear and come out washed out or over-dark; FBXLoader and ICC handling changed earlier.
risks.symptom: colors washed out or faded on loaded models and textures while untextured geometry looks right

source.note: A loaded model must look like its source in the engine (judgement line of the glTF node).

engine.says: `Texture.encoding` has been replaced with `Texture.colorSpace`
`THREE.ColorManagement.enabled` is now `true` by default.
`FBXLoader` now correctly sets the texture encoding.
Embedded color space data (ICC-profiles) in texture images will now be ignored.

risks.title: Renderer output color space default
risks.breaks: r152 replaced outputEncoding with outputColorSpace defaulting to SRGBColorSpace, so a game that never set outputEncoding now gets sRGB output and every frame shifts in tone.
risks.symptom: the whole frame is brighter, washed out or differently saturated, every capture differs

source.note: Hero must stay readable against the background in a grayscale capture.

engine.says: `WebGLRenderer.outputEncoding` has been replaced with `WebGLRenderer.outputColorSpace`
`WebGLRenderer.gammaOutput` has been removed.

risks.title: Tone mapping moved to the output pass
risks.breaks: Inline tone mapping now applies only when rendering to screen, so post-processed games lose tone mapping unless they add OutputPass; the default is NoToneMapping.
risks.symptom: post-processed scenes look flat, blown out or lose contrast; scenes without post-processing are unchanged

source.note: Lightness contrast between hero and surroundings is the readability floor.

engine.says: The inline tone mapping controlled via `WebGLRenderer.toneMapping` only works when rendering to screen now
The default value of `WebGLRenderer.toneMapping` is now `NoToneMapping`.

risks.title: Physically correct light units by default
risks.breaks: r155 set useLegacyLights to false, so light intensities are read in physical units and scenes tuned for legacy units render much darker.
risks.symptom: the scene is much darker or lights look dim after the upgrade, geometry is unchanged

source.note: The default rig adds ambient, diffuse and specular terms; a directional light plays the sun.

engine.says: `WebGLRenderer.useLegacyLights` is now set to `false` by default and deprecated.
`WebGLRenderer.physicallyCorrectLights = true` is now `WebGLRenderer.useLegacyLights = false`.

risks.title: Point and spot light decay default
risks.breaks: PointLight and SpotLight decay now defaults to 2, so lights with no decay set fall off faster.
risks.symptom: areas lit by point or spot lights turn dark away from the light; directional light areas unchanged

source.note: Fill and rim strengths are per-game choices on top of the default rig.

engine.says: The `decay` property of `PointLight` and `SpotLight` has now a physically correct default value (`2`).

risks.title: Shadow classes left the public API
risks.breaks: LightShadow, SpotLightShadow and DirectionalLightShadow left the public API, so code that constructs them throws.
risks.symptom: page error naming a Shadow class, or shadows vanish

source.note: Shadows come from a depth map with a small bias; acne and peter panning are the two failure looks.

engine.says: `LightShadow` has been removed from the public API.
`SpotLightShadow` and `DirectionalLightShadow` have been removed from the public API.

risks.title: PBR and Lambert shading changes
risks.breaks: Standard and Physical materials became more correct (less shiny when rough), envMap is converted to PMREM, IBL preserves energy, and Lambert moved to per-fragment shading.
risks.symptom: materials look less shiny, metals brighter, or shading smoother; small diffs spread over every lit surface

source.note: Global illumination choice decides how indirect light reaches the scene.

engine.says: shaders are now more correct and may result in less shiny renders for models using rough materials.
The `envMap` property of `MeshStandardMaterial` and `MeshPhysicalMaterial` is now internally converted to a PMREM.
`MeshLambertMaterial` now uses per-fragment shading.

risks.title: examples/js removed and import maps required
risks.breaks: r148 removed examples/js, so script-tag addons such as GLTFLoader or OrbitControls stop existing; ES module imports of three need an import map.
risks.symptom: page error "is not a constructor" or "Failed to resolve module specifier", 404 on an examples/js file, nothing loads

source.note: Every asset path a scene requests must exist and load.

engine.says: The `examples/js` directory has been removed.
now requires the usage of an import map to resolve the `three` bare import specifier.

risks.title: GLTFLoader result shape and material defaults
risks.breaks: GLTFLoader returns a Group instead of a Scene, sets depthWrite false on transparent materials, keeps node order, and dropped spec-gloss materials.
risks.symptom: transparent parts sort wrong, some models turn grey or black, or code walking gltf.scene breaks

source.note: glTF top-level elements are scenes, nodes, meshes, materials, textures, skins, animations.

engine.says: `GLTFLoader` now returns an instance of `Group` instead of `Scene`.
`GLTFLoader` now sets `depthWrite` to `false` for transparent materials.
Support for the `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` extensions has been removed from `GLTFLoader`

risks.title: Legacy Geometry removed from core
risks.breaks: r125 removed Geometry and Face3 from core, so games building meshes with THREE.Geometry throw and draw nothing.
risks.symptom: page error "THREE.Geometry is not a constructor", empty scene

source.note: Meshes are indexed buffers optimized in a fixed order.

engine.says: `Geometry` has been removed from the core.
`Mesh`, `Line` and `Points` no longer support raycasting with `Geometry`.

risks.title: Draco, Basis and KTX2 decoder paths
risks.breaks: Draco and Basis decoder libraries moved under examples/jsm/libs and KTX2Loader needs an updated transcoder, so compressed models fail to decode.
risks.symptom: failed request for a decoder .wasm or .js, compressed models missing

source.note: glTF files are optimized with gltfpack; compression is part of the pipeline.

engine.says: Users of ammo.js, Draco and Basis have to update their import paths
`KTX2Loader` requires an updated version of the Basis Universal transcoder

risks.title: Controls moved to pointer events and explicit DOM element
risks.breaks: OrbitControls, TrackballControls and TransformControls use pointer events, stop listening to keys by default, and require the renderer canvas as domElement.
risks.symptom: camera no longer follows drag, wheel or keys; frames after input match frames before it; page error on domElement

source.note: Read input as actions in one handler; keyboard-layout swaps must still move the game.

engine.says: `OrbitControls`, `TrackballControls` and `TransformControls` now use Pointer Events.
`OrbitControls` no longer listens to key events by default.
The second constructor parameter `domElement` of `OrbitControls`
`DragControls`, `OrbitControls` and `TrackballControls` now use pointer events for touch interaction.

risks.title: Raycaster defaults
risks.breaks: Raycaster intersection is recursive by default and honors invisible objects, so clicks can pick children or hidden meshes.
risks.symptom: clicks select the wrong object, hover highlights flicker, picking hits invisible meshes

source.note: Each screen state enables its own input context; two contexts never claim one input at one priority.

engine.says: The `recursive` parameter of `Raycaster.intersectObject()` and `Raycaster.intersectObjects()` is now `true` by default.
`Raycaster` honors now invisible 3D objects in intersection tests.

risks.title: Audio.startTime removed
risks.breaks: Audio.startTime was removed in favor of Audio.play(delay).
risks.symptom: sound starts at the wrong moment or not at all; possible page error

source.note: Audio opens on the first user gesture.

engine.says: `Audio.startTime` has been removed.

risks.title: AudioContext left suspended
risks.breaks: A game or engine change that creates its AudioContext at load without resume() on a gesture stays silent under browser autoplay policy.
risks.symptom: silent game, console warning that the AudioContext was not allowed to start

source.note: At least one context, resumed after scripted play, zero blocked media.

risks.title: Simulation step tied to frame time
risks.breaks: When an upgrade changes the render loop or clock, a game that steps physics by frame delta drifts: early frames match, later frames diverge.
risks.symptom: first captures match, later captures differ more and more; the replayed route ends somewhere else

source.note: Same seed and same input give the same run; one extra random call shifts every later roll.

risks.title: CannonPhysics removed
risks.breaks: The CannonPhysics addon was removed.
risks.symptom: page error naming CannonPhysics, bodies do not move

source.note: Stacked bodies settle to zero velocity and sleep.

engine.says: `CannonPhysics` has been removed.

risks.title: Save format without a version
risks.breaks: An upgrade PR that renames serialized classes or fields (Math to MathUtils, toJSON shapes) breaks saves written by the old build unless the save carries a version and a migration.
risks.symptom: progress or settings lost after reload on the head build; JSON parse page error

source.note: Every JSON the run writes to localStorage carries an integer version; old samples must load.

engine.says: `Math` has been renamed to `MathUtils`

risks.title: Results differ across renderers and machines
risks.breaks: Float results differ between browsers, GPUs and SwiftShader, so a head build can pass on one renderer and fail on another.
risks.symptom: PASS on SwiftShader, FAIL on a GPU or another browser, or the reverse

source.note: The same input record must hash the same per step on different browsers and devices.

risks.title: WebGL 2 by default, WebGL 1 removed
risks.breaks: r118 creates a WebGL 2 context by default, WebGL 1 was deprecated and removed in r163, and SkinnedMesh no longer runs on WebGL 1.
risks.symptom: blank or black canvas, context creation error, skinned characters missing on old GPUs

source.note: A material template must compile and draw one frame without errors.

engine.says: `WebGLRenderer` automatically creates a WebGL 2 rendering context now
WebGL 1 support in `WebGLRenderer` is now deprecated and will be removed in r163.
`SkinnedMesh` is not supported with WebGL 1 anymore.
